properties.summary: Environmental Health & Safety violation issued on 4/18/2024 to SENECA RESOURCES CO LLC in Middlebury Township, Tioga county. 78.85(a)5 - CASING AND CEMENTING - CEMENT STANDARDS - The operator failed prevent gas flow in the annulus.  In areas of known shallow gas producing zones, gas block additives and low fluid loss slurries shall be used.
properties.content:
Report Details
Inspection Client: SENECA RESOURCES CO LLC
Violation Type: Environmental Health & Safety
Violation Date: 4/18/2024
Violation Code: 78.85(a)5 - CASING AND CEMENTING - CEMENT STANDARDS - The operator failed prevent gas flow in the annulus. In areas of known shallow gas producing zones, gas block additives and low fluid loss slurries shall be used.
Violation ID: 8184614
Permit API: 117-22215
Unconventional: Yes
County: Tioga
Municipality: Middlebury Township
Inspection Type: Routine/Complete Inspection
Inspection Date: 4/18/2024
Comments: Onsite at 12:22. The weather was windy, cool and cloudy. On 4/17/2024, Seneca reported to the Department the presence of combustible gas (e.g., 60 bubbles per minute) outside of the surface casing string at the Bauer 849 66HU gas well. This inspection was conducted at the Bauer 849 69 HU gas well in response to that report. At the time of the inspection, Nextier Completion Solutions (Hydraulic Fracturing Company) was preparing the wells and well area for the upcoming completion activities. The annulus vents were open and checked for the presence or absence of combustible gas with an Altair 5X Multi Gas Meter that was calibrated on 04-01-2024. The results of this annulus vent monitoring were as follows: Conductor by Surface casing (20" x 13 3/8") – 21% LEL (lower explosion limit) and 0% Methane/Volume Surface by Intermediate casing (13 3/8" x 9 5/8") – 0% LEL and 0% Methane/Volume Intermediate by Production casing (9 5/8" x 5 1/2") – 100% LEL and 11% Methane/Volume The Department's investigation of the Bauer 849 69HU well found that combustible gas is currently venting outside of the surface casing string. This is a violation of the Department's regulations relating to Cement Standards, 25 Pa. Code ¿¿78a.85(a)(5), which provides: "When cementing surface casing or coal protective casing, the operator shall use cement that meets or exceeds the ASTM International C 150, Type I, II, or III Standard or API Specification 10. The cement must also: (5) Prevent gas flow in the annulus. In areas of known shallow gas producing zones, gas block additives and low fluid loss slurries shall be used." Please note that, because Seneca provided a self-reported notification, no violation was cited for 25 Pa. Code ¿¿78a.86 (defective cement), for the annuli where combustible gas was detected during this inspection. However, Seneca is still required to comply with the Department's regulations, 25 Pa. Code ¿¿78a. 86, which provides: "In a well that has defective, insufficient or improperly cemented casing, the operator shall report the defect to the Department within 24 hours of discovery by the operator and shall correct the defect. The operator shall correct the defect or submit a plan to correct the defect for approval by the Department within 30 days. If the defect cannot be corrected or an alternate method is not approved by the Department, the well shall be plugged under ¿¿ 78.91 – 78.98 (related to plugging)." Therefore, please provide a written response detailing how Seneca intends to comply with this regulation, including information regarding the suspected source of stray gas, by 5/17/2024. Offsite at 13:42.

Comments: This admin inspection is being conducted in response to review of 3rd party consultant, Moody and Associates, Inc., investigation report for the Manack 2 Well Site in Rostraver Township, Westmoreland County. Review of DEP inspections, Moody's investigation report and ES plans for the well site were conducted. In IR 3011479 and IR 3310984, drill cutting pit locations and waste manifests were requested and were unable to be obtained, due to the well site transfer from Atlas Resources to Diversified Oil and Gas. Diversified OG suspected the drill cuttings were land farmed which corroborated with the well site's ES plan. However, in Moody's report, they identified the approximate locations of the cuttings pit by increasing the the vertical exaggeration of the terrain in Good Earth and confirming with land owner upon a site visit conducted March 19th, 2020. The drill pit was located approximately 50 ft northwest of the well. Results reported by DEP and Moody's indicated elevated metal concentrations and pH levels in several locations around the well site. Due to reported lab results and identification of drill pit by Moody, the Department recommends that the Operator evaluate the integrity of the drill pit. Based on DEP sample results and Moody's investigation report, violations are being issued under 78.61 and 78.62.

properties.content:
Report Details
Inspection Client: TRINITY MINERAL PARTNERS LLC
Violation Type: Environmental Health & Safety
Violation Date: 8/12/2026
Violation Code: 78.54 - GENERAL REQUIREMENTS - Operator failed to control and dispose of fluids, residual waste and drill cuttings, including tophole water, brines, drilling fluids, drilling muds, stimulation fluids, well servicing fluids, oil, and production fluids in a manner that prevents pollution of the waters of the Commonwealth.
Violation ID: 8284377
Permit API: 123-46784
Unconventional: No
County: Warren
Municipality: Sugar Grove Township
Inspection Type: Routine/Complete Inspection
Inspection Date: 8/12/2026
Comments: Kyle Miller of Trinity Mineral Partners (TMP) reported a release of produced fluids at TMP's Brown Hill Road tank battery. The tank battery consists of five 210 bbl stock tanks (# 1053, 1054, 1055, 1056, 1057), a separator, gas meter, burner, and buried brine tank. The Brown Hill Church Lease, Lyszaz Lease, and R Brown Lease are plumbed to this tank battery.It was reported that lightning from recent thunderstorms must have struck the tanks, ignited combustible contents, and caused an explosion that expanded and ruptured four out of the five tanks. The released fluid flowed through the ruptures and into the secondary containment area. It was reported that at the time of the release, the stock tanks were mostly empty but did contain some sludge from prior storage of produced fluids.Brian Bennett of TMP was onsite at the time of this inspection to discuss cleanup expectations with Evan Bruce (WQS) and I (Mathew Haemer - WQS). Brian estimated that the volume of the released fluids was approximately 4 bbl. Brian explained that he had been working on mixing sawdust with the sludge that had filled the containment area and had begun to remove the saturated sawdust to temporary storage in barrels staged inside the secondary containment area.At the time of this inspection, the buried brine tank was nearly empty. The majority of the release pooled around the buried brine tank. Brine was not reported to be a suspected component of this release. However, elevated SPC readings were observed both in the sawdust/sludge mixture (5,350 uS/cm) and in the soils of the secondary containment area's western end (8,900 uS/cm).Two groundhog holes were observed in the northwest corner of the secondary containment area. Elevated SPC readings (4,140/12,250 uS/cm) were observed in the soil inside of the groundhog holes. This indicates that at one point in time, brine discharged into the secondary containment area rose to a level sufficient to spill over into the holes, and from that point migrate outside of containment. A storage yard has been constructed downslope of the tank battery. HDPE pipe is scattered at one end, and spare pump jacks at the other. Coincidentally, the soil is visibly wet beneath the area where the HDPE pipe is scattered. Elevated SPC of soils (1,468 uS/cm) was observed where the pipe is scattered. The disturbed earth above the pipe and pump jacks also had elevated SPC readings (1,346 uS/cm). A violation for failure to construct and maintain a method of secondary containment which satisfies requirements under 40 CFR 112 is being cited due to the evidence that brine was able to migrate through the secondary containment wall via the groundhog holes and/or through permeating the earthen containment.The quantity of the release exceeds the 1 bbl threshold set forth in the Department's spill policy, therefore either the Act 2 or Alternative Remediation Process is required. It is requested that the source and extent of the release be identified.

Violation ID: 8241088
Permit API: 015-23892
Unconventional: Yes
County: Bradford

Inspection Type: Administrative/File Review
Inspection Date: 7/14/2025
Comments: At 1945 hours on 7/13/2025, the Department received notification of a well control incident at the Broadleaf Holdings 7H unconventional gas well. Reportedly, Repsol personnel observed fluids from the well overtopping containment while stimulating the well. The purpose of this Administrative inspection report is to document the Department's initial response to the notification using the SubSAIR mobile app. In response to the notification, the Department deployed Emergency Response Team (ERT) members Jonathan Pennings and Scotty Brown to the site. Jonathan Pennings arrived at 2135 hours on 7/13/2025 and Scotty Brown arrived at 2058 hours on 7/13/2025. Upon arrival, an unknown amount of fluids was observed outside of containment. During the initial response, booms were deployed and earthen berms were constructed in an attempt to mitigate runoff. Reportedly, "halfway through the frac," the well pressure dropped from approximately 9000 psi to 3000 psi and all three annuli were compromised leading to a fluids release from the well to the surface. Further inquiry revealed that the breach occurred while stimulating Stage 50 of 67 at approximately 18:05 hours. In response, Repsol attempted to set a kill plug below the breach, but the plug got stuck near surface. At that time, it was determined the a Coil Tubing Unit would be necessary to drill out the stuck plug and set a new kill plug. Reportedly, no combustible gas was detected at this time. At 01:15 hours on 7/14/2025, CUDD Well Control (CUDD) and Mansfield Crane arrive to the site. At 0331, CUDD setup water cannons for safety purposes. Water management efforts continued on the pad. At 0900 on 7/14/2025, Kyle Menc (Oil and Gas Inspector) arrived to the site to continue the Department's oversight efforts. Jonathan Pennings left the site at 0640 hours on 7/14/2025 and Scotty Brown left the site at 0930 hours on 7/14/2025. Additional details regarding the Department's initial response to the notification are provided in the PADEP-Emergency Response Incident Report generated by Scotty Brown. Based on the findings made during the Department's initial response to the notification, violations have been cited for ¿¿78a.73(a) and ¿¿78a.85(c). It should be noted that, because Repsol previously provided a self-reported notification, no violation was cited for ¿¿78a.86, which states: "In a well that has defective, insufficient or improperly cemented casing, the operator shall report the defect to the Department within 24 hours of discovery by the operator and shall correct the defect. The operator shall correct the defect or submit a plan to correct the defect for approval by the Department within 30 days. If the defect cannot be corrected or an alternate method is not approved by the Department, the well shall be plugged under ¿¿ 78a.91 - 78a.98 (related to plugging)." As a result of these findings, please provide a written response by 8/8/2025 detailing the root cause or causes that lead to loss of well control and corrective actions that Repsol proposes to implement to prevent similar failures in the future. In addition, although a violation of ¿¿78a.86 has not been cited, the written response should also include information regarding how Repsol intends to comply with this regulation.

Violation ID: 8286046
Permit API: 125-23924
Unconventional: Yes
County: Washington
Municipality: Somerset Township
Inspection Type: Complaint Inspection
Inspection Date: 8/19/2026
Comments: On August 19, 2026, the Department conducted a complaint inspection of the Cecil 2-P229 OG Well in regard to CTS 400392.The findings are as follows:At the time of the inspection, the Department did not observe an Act 9 sign. The Department recommends the operator install an Act 9 sign in accordance with 78a55. The Department also did not observe an Emergency Response Plan (ERP). The Department recommends the operator ensure an ERP is onsite in accordance with 78a55.At the time of the inspection the well was located in an open agricultural field. The access road appeared stabilized. No erosion or sedimentation issues were observed at the time of the inspection.Upon inspection of the production equipment, the well appeared equipped for production. A well tag and well posting were present onsite appeared to have all information in accordance with OGA3211(G) and OGA3211(H). There were no observed leaks or discharges of fluid at the surface around the wellhead.There appeared to be 3 total production tanks onsite. Upon further inspection, it appeared the white poly tank was connected and in use. The tank appeared to be in sound condition with no observed leaks or discharges of fluid were observed around this tank.Two metal tanks were also present onsite but did not appear to be in use at the time of the inspection. Upon further inspection of the 2 metal tanks, one of the tanks appeared to be severely corroded with multiple holes in the tank observed. The Department observed fluid flowing down the side of the tank. A conductivity reading of this fluid was obtained and was "OR" (Over detectable range, >20mS). Upon inspection of the ground surrounding the corroded production tank, the Department observed orange staining and saturated dirt/gravel. Conductivity readings were taken in the area of staining and saturation with readings of 12.78mS, 9.24mS, 4.37mS, and 1.82mS being obtained. These readings are elevated in comparison to the background conductivity reading obtained of 0.19mS. Based on the Department's observations and conductivity readings, it appears a release has/is occurring from the corroded production tank.Prior to leaving the site, the Department spoke with operator representative Robert Inghram and informed him of the Department's observations of an apparent release. Mr. Inghram stated the metal tanks have been disconnected and empty for several years. The Department recommended remediation of the spill and removal of the production tanks as they are no longer in use and heavily corroded. Mr. Inghram stated he would get a contractor to begin the work as soon as possible.Based on today's inspection, violations are being issued for the observed release, production equipment onsite not in use, no ERP onsite, and no Act 9 Sign onsite.

Unconventional: No

Inspection Type: Routine/Complete Inspection
Inspection Date: 4/13/2026
Comments: On 4/13/2026, the Department conducted a routine inspection at the Holchin 2 well plugging site in North Union Township, Fayette County. This inspection was conducted in response to a Notice of Intent (NOI) to plug the well, which was submitted by the operator on 3/16/2026. Tyler Hinkle (Next Level Energy) was on site during this inspection. The following was observed during the inspection:Upon arrival, the Department spoke with Next Level Energy representative Tyler Hinkle, who was on site to make minor repairs to the temporary BMPs installed on site and to remove an excavator from site. Hinkle identified during this inspection evidence of third-party disturbance due to livestock grazing on site. The Department recommends that the operator document any third-party disturbances occurring on site, and take reasonable efforts to stop them and prevent accelerated erosion from occurring on site. Temporary Erosion and sedimentation controls are installed downslope of the access road and well site. No evidence of accelerated erosion was observed on site during this inspection. The site E and S/Restoration plans are available in a mailbox on site. The site appears to be staged for well plugging operations, however no machinery related to well plugging is on site at the time of inspection. The gas well is disconnected from the production equipment. No evidence of a spill, such as staining, was observed on site during this inspection. The API number was not visible anywhere on site. While on site, the Department reviewed the site E and S/Restoration plans. The Rock Construction Entrance (RCE) is not installed in the location shown in the E and S plan drawing (photos 4 and 15). Although an overall BMP layout drawing exists, the plans state that E and S controls are to be installed at contractor's discretion. At the time of this inspection, the E and S controls appear to be installed on site in a manner that is preventing accelerated erosion and sedimentation from occurring. The Department recommends that that the operator monitor the site and install additional temporary E and S controls as necessary in order to minimize the potential for accelerated erosion and sedimentation to occur. The Department recommends that the site E and S/Restoration plans are kept updated via redlining with the BMP's currently installed on site. Based on observations from this inspection, violations shall be issued for failure to failure to follow the E and S plan.An additional violation shall be issued in IR 4177612 for failure to post the API number on site.

The completions operations have ceased on Pad B and the snubbing rigs and their associated equipment have been removed from the pad. I met with EQT representative Zac Subra upon arriving on Pad B. A representative from Creston Environmental was present on location as well. A crew was working on installing the GPUs on the pad. Trenches were being dug for the flow lines which will run from the well heads to the GPUs on the west side of the pad. A large trench was present at the well heads. Some fluid was seeping into this trench from the fill material surrounding the well cellar for well B-11H. The electrical conductivity (EC) of this fluid was 2.45 mS/cm. A vacuum truck was sucking up this fluid during this inspection. The Department recommends continuing to vacuum up any elevated EC fluid found on the pad surface or during excavation on the pad. The modular aboveground storage structure (MASS) was empty during this inspection. A work crew was beginning to disassemble the MASS during this inspection. The north central area of the well pad has been excavated. One area is a long horizontal area approximately two feet of the north stormwater channel. The EC of the fluid here was 3.35 to 5.41 mS/cm. Another excavated area is to the southwest. According to Mr. Subra, EQT believes that the produced fluid that had been released to this area flowed along an area that had previously been excavated in association with a release that occurred during drilling operations on the well pad. Mr. Subra also said that the northwest area of the well pad where clamshell boxes had led to a release in the dancefloor area has been fully excavated. Additional excavation would still need to occur in the north central area of the well pad as well as in the northeast corner of the pad where the MASS still is present, he also stated. The lined sump remains at the east outlet of the north stormwater channel.Violations remain outstanding for the reported release of produced fluid to the surface of Pad B.

Permit API: 117-22026
Unconventional: Yes
County: Tioga
Municipality: Liberty Twp
Inspection Type: Incident- Response to Accident or Event
Inspection Date: 2019-02-27
Comments: Inspection conducted in response to a spill notification received yesterday 2/26/19 about a release of an estimated 10 gallons of produced water that had occurred at 1730 the same day. Mike Deming of SWN met me on location upon my arrival. He explained that an 18-wheeler off-loading produced water from a battery of frac tanks had inadvertently pumped produced water out of the truck into the tank instead of pumping it out of the tank and into the truck. This activated a pressure relief valve on the truck which led to the release of the produced water. Mr. Deming said that a vacuum truck on site immediately sucked up the fluid and gravel from the pad surface was scraped with a skid steer and placed into a container for disposal. At the time of this inspection, the site was snow-covered and the impacted gravel material had already been removed. During the inspection, a zipper frac was in process on the 10H and 5H wells. The site was in good shape overall. The secondary containment appeared to be fully intact with no visible damage. Fresh water was being pumped in from a FWI as well as trucked in to the site. Violations noted and considered immediately corrected.

properties.summary: Environmental Health & Safety violation issued on 6/14/2024 to QUESTA PETRO CO in East Huntingdon Township, Westmoreland county. 78.57(a) - CONTROL, STORAGE AND DISPOSAL OF PRODUCTION FLUIDS - Operator failed to collect the brine and other fluids produced during operation, service and plugging of the well in a tank, pit or a series of pits or tanks, or other device approved by the Department or Operator discharged brine or other fluids on or into the ground or into waters of the Commonwealth.
properties.content:
Report Details
Inspection Client: QUESTA PETRO CO
Violation Type: Environmental Health & Safety
Violation Date: 6/14/2024
Violation Code: 78.57(a) - CONTROL, STORAGE AND DISPOSAL OF PRODUCTION FLUIDS - Operator failed to collect the brine and other fluids produced during operation, service and plugging of the well in a tank, pit or a series of pits or tanks, or other device approved by the Department or Operator discharged brine or other fluids on or into the ground or into waters of the Commonwealth.
Violation ID: 8191185
Permit API: 129-26032
Unconventional: No
County: Westmoreland
Municipality: East Huntingdon Township
Inspection Type: Routine/Complete Inspection
Inspection Date: 6/14/2024
Comments: On June 14, 2024 the Department conducted a Routine Inspection of the Joseph A Negri 1 well located in East Huntington Township, Westmoreland County. During a previous inspection (IR 3723492) the Department observed a drum on site with a Methanol label on it. At that time the Department requested the operator provide information by 3/29/24 on what exactly is in the drum and what it is being used for, the Department also requested that the Operator remove all equipment not necessary for production. The Department has not received a response from the Operator in regards to this site.At the time of this inspection, the well site was exhibiting greater than 70% uniform and adequate vegetative growth with no accelerated erosion or sedimentation issues observed. A well tag with all required information posted on it was fixed to the wellhead. No fluid leaks or fluid discharges were observed coming from or near the wellhead. Some production equipment onsite that appeared to be in production due to the gauge attached to it had an open pipe close to the ground. A soil conductivity reading was taken at the edge of the well site in some vegetation as a background (0.0074 mS) and then a reading was taken directly next to the piping (0.409 mS) and then a little further back from this piping (0.382 mS). The production tank also had some wet marks coming from the top of the tank and the wet marks can be seen going down the tank towards the ground in areas. Soil conductivity readings were taken at the base of the production tank below areas where the wet marks were observed on the tank (0.1483 mS and 0.1405 mS). The drum of methanol was observed to still be on site, not in secondary containment and fluid can be seen sitting at the top of it with air bubbles forming from what may be a small hole or crack in the top of the barrel. Soil conductivity readings were taken at the base of the drum (0.096 mS), as well as in the fluid sitting at the top of the drum (0.620 mS).The soil conductivity readings taken near the open pipe and at the base of the production tank are elevated in comparison to the background soil conductivity reading and subjugate that there is some sort of release contaminating the soil in both areas. The reading at the base of the Methanol drum is comparable to the background, but the fluid sitting at the top and the air bubbles seen indicate that there may be a leak at the top of the drum which currently has the potential to reach the ground. While onsite, the Department spoke with Dave Lindahl of Mountain View to let him know about the elevated readings by the production equipment and production tank and informed him about the possible hole at the top of the Methanol Drum. The Department recommended the drum be removed or put in secondary containment as soon as possible and recommended they determine how the two leaks occurred, stop them, remove all contaminated soil, replace it with new top soil, and seed/mulch. Dave stated that someone would be onsite on 6/17/24 to begin working on all of this. The Department is recommending the Operator either remove this drum or put it within secondary containment by COB June 28, 2024. Based on todays inspection, violations shall be issued at this time for failure to remove production equipment not currently in use and for a release from production equipment.

Report Details
Inspection Client: DIVERSIFIED PROD LLC
Violation Type: Environmental Health & Safety
Violation Date: 3/11/2024
Violation Code: 78.53 - EROSION AND SEDIMENT CONTROL - Operator failed to design, implement and maintain best management practices and an erosion and sediment control plan in accordance with 25 Pa. Code Chapter 102, during and after earthmoving or soil disturbing activities, including the activities related to siting, drilling, completing, producing, servicing and plugging, constructing, utilizing and restoring the site and access road.
Violation ID: 8179690
Permit API: 125-22817
Unconventional: No
County: Washington
Municipality: Fallowfield Township
Inspection Type: Follow-up Inspection
Inspection Date: 3/11/2024
Comments: On 03/11/2024, a follow up inspection was conducted at the Molek F19 well site following violations issued on 12/08/2023 (IR 3657799, Enforcement 419234). I was accompanied by Environmental Trainees Olivia Holley, Madison Raviart, and Christina Mauri (PA DEP).On 12/08/2023, violations of 102.11(a), 102.22(a)2ii, and 78.53 were issued as outstanding for the access road. Inspection from 12/28/2023 noted that the violations were still open, however the operator was in compliance with schedule. On 01/24/2024, the violations were outstanding (IR 3701625). The following was observed:Some stabilization was used along the upper portion of the access road. Several areas throughout the entire access road did not have stabilization on the open soils. I recommend that stabilization is applied (Photos 1-4). Some areas had vegetation establishing (Photos 2, 4, 5).The channel that runs along the access road did not have rip rap or stabilization. Accelerated erosion and sediment accumulation were noted within this channel, which leads to several culverts along the road (Photo 6).The upper culvert, located at 40.113707 -79.966213, had sediment accumulation within the collection point. I recommend that this is addressed (Photo 7). The culvert located at 40.11300, -79.96751 had large amounts of sediment accumulated within the collection point. The culvert was not able to be seen due to the large amount of sediment within this area (Photos 8, 9). Accelerated erosion was noted within the accumulated sediment (Photo 9). The outlet point of this culvert was covered by the roads gravel/dirt, which was causing accelerated erosion and sediment transport towards the vegetation (Photos 10-12). I recommend that this is addressed. The culvert leading to the collection box was not functioning. Sediment was accumulated and an entry point into the pipe was approximately 99% covered. Accelerated erosion and sedimentation throughout the area and vegetation were noted leading from the channel towards the collection box. There was some sediment laden water within this box. This outlets into the vegetation, where sediment accumulation was noted. The vegetation was accumulating water, which leads towards the stream within the wood line (Photos 13-19). The lower culvert outlets into a channel. Sediment accumulation was noted within the channel. I recommend that rip rap is used within this channel, as this leads directly to the stream (Photos 20, 21).The culverts along the first portion of the access road, near the site gate, were not cleaned out. Potholes along the road were not addressed. Channelization was noted leading from the potholes off of the road. The beginning of the access road, where it meets the township road, was not addressed. This area was previously displaying high levels of flow, leading onto the township road, and depositing sediment. This was noted within IR 3701625, photos 24 and 15 (Photos 22-25). The violations issued on 01/24/2024, IR 3701625, remain outstanding.
